extracted.intended_audience: The people of New York / citizens debating ratification of the U.S. Constitution (general 18th‑century public)
extracted.subtask_description: Political-argument pamphlet (Federalist Papers Nos. 7–9) giving reasons why disunion would lead to interstate hostility, standing armies, loss of liberty, and why a larger united republic will suppress faction and insurrection. Intended to persuade voters/delegates to support the proposed Constitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vicinity (nearness) produces natural enmity
rubrics_metrics.description: From long observation of the progress of society it is 'a sort of axiom in politics, that vicinity or nearness of situation, constitutes nations natural enemies.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proximity creates secret jealousy and dispositions to aggrandize at neighbors' expense; this tendency argues for a confederate republic or union to extinguish those differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial disputes as a primary source of interstate hostility
rubrics_metrics.description: Territorial disputes have at all times been one of the most fertile sources of hostility among nations; the U.S. has vast unsettled Western territory and discordant claims that would be revived by disunion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without a common umpire, competing claims (e.g., crown lands, post‑Revolution unsettled grants) would lead to heated contestation, difficulty of apportionment, and potentially resort to force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of a federal umpire/judge invites appeal to the sword
rubrics_metrics.description: In the wide field of Western territory there is ample theater for hostile pretensions 'without any umpire or common judge to interpose' between contending parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past examples (e.g., Connecticut/Pennsylvania; Connecticut/Vermont disputes) show that even when legal mechanisms exist, dissatisfaction and force can follow; a federal authority reduces this danger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitions of commerce will generate contention
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate states pursuing peculiar commercial policies would produce distinctions, preferences, exclusions, and discontent; states would be tempted to escape local disadvantages by seeking the benefits of neighbors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Habit of equal privileges increases sensitivity to perceived injuries; trade infractions and reprisals would escalate into outrages and wars; commercial regulation that makes one state 'tributary' to another breeds resentment (example: NY duties affecting CT/NJ).

rubrics_metrics.name: States will denominate independent sovereign acts as injuries
rubrics_metrics.description: We should be ready to denominate injuries those things which were in reality the justifiable acts of independent sovereignties consulting a distinct interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When each state pursues its own commercial interest, legitimate measures by one will be seen as oppressive by neighbors, increasing likelihood of conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public debt apportionment is a source of discord
rubrics_metrics.description: The public debt of the Union would be a further cause of collision: apportionment initially and progressive extinguishment afterward would produce ill-humor and animosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Difficulties in agreeing on a fair rule (none free from objections), divergent interests (creditor vs non‑creditor states), procrastination, delinquencies, and failure to pay would provoke complaints, recriminations, and risk to peace and credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws violating private contracts provoke interstate retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws in violation of private contracts, as aggressions on the rights of those states whose citizens are injured, may be considered another probable source of hostility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disgraceful or unjust state legislation (examples cited) provokes retaliation; in extreme cases this would not be a 'war of parchment' but of the sword.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incompatible alliances with foreign nations endanger collective peace
rubrics_metrics.description: The probability of incompatible alliances between different states and different foreign nations would entangle America in European politics and wars; divided parts would be prey to artifices of foreign powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A weak or merely league‑based connection cannot prevent jarring alliances and foreign machinations; 'Divide et impera' is the motto of powers hostile to a divided America.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disunion will lead to standing armies and strengthened executives
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent war and constant apprehension would produce standing armies; weaker states would adopt disciplined troops and fortifications, and strengthen the executive arm, tending toward monarchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standing armies are both a likely consequence of disunion and an engine that increases executive power at the expense of legislative authority, threatening civil and political rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of warfare in a disunited, lightly fortified country will be predatory
rubrics_metrics.description: In this country the want of fortifications and militias would facilitate inroads; populous states could easily overrun less populous neighbors, making war desultory and predatory—'PLUNDER and devastation ever march in the train of irregulars.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a pattern of war would devastate individuals, produce continual alarm, and eventually compel recourse to institutions that reduce liberty for safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic insulation (insular situation) reduces need for large militaries
rubrics_metrics.description: An insular situation (as with Great Britain) lessens internal standing armies and helps preserve liberty; Union gives America a similar advantage due to distance from Europe and local colonial powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Union is preserved, extensive military establishments are unnecessary; disunion would subject parts to continental-style militarization and attendant loss of liberties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlargement of the orbit (a larger republic) suppresses faction and insurrection
rubrics_metrics.description: A firm Union will be of the utmost moment to peace and liberty as a barrier against domestic faction and insurrection; enlargement of the orbit (consolidating smaller states into a great confederacy) helps suppress faction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modern principles—distribution of power into departments, legislative balances and checks, independent judiciary, and popular representation—combined with a larger scope, enable republican government to avoid the rapid revolutions of small republics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern constitutional devices ameliorate defects of republics
rubrics_metrics.description: The regular distribution of power, legislative balances and checks, courts with judges during good behavior, and representation by elected deputies are new or improved means to retain republican excellences and lessen imperfections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These institutions, especially when applied within an enlarged orbit (union), are presented as effective safeguards against the disorders that afflicted ancient petty republics.
